ordered_source_facts.fact: screen_device::vblank_begin calls video_manager::frame_update before screen-specific callbacks and screen_vblank(1).
video_manager::frame_update performs OSD input/UI/render work, then calls MACHINE_NOTIFY_FRAME.
The input manager registers a frame notifier; its callback rebuilds port digital cache from fields, while port reads return that cached value.

The Mega Drive screen uses zero configured vblank duration and a screen_vblank callback; its rising edge starts VDP EOF/scanline-timer work after the frame-update call. The VDP VINT callback asserts 68K IRQ level 6.
VDP scanline work raises its VINT path at the configured IRQ6 scanline and schedules the interrupt assertion.
The guest level-6 handler calls ControllerPoll before incrementing DEBUG_FRAME_TOKEN.
ControllerPoll stores sampled input; mainline later consumes the frame token and passes INPUT_HELD into GameplayStep.
Genewhip's route field callback runs after a newly published emulated field is observed and PCM is drained.

The retained D-118 695-to-697 observation cannot supply that missing source correspondence without circular calibration.

parent_source_audit.fact: Frame callbacks normally execute in registration order; input ports initialize before create_custom. This alone does not order every Lua callback relative to cache refresh.
The B request comes from the completed-source-step write tap; the frame notifier handles only meta C transitions. No B delay may be inferred from the frame-notifier counter.

For the default timing path, EOF resets the VDP scanline counter to -1, the first scanline callback increments it to 0, and IRQ6 is scheduled at its configured scanline. This is a distinct stage from the native publication callback.

The native model publishes at active-line end and schedules VINT at that line plus the modeled offset; the session callback follows publication after a run boundary, rather than defining a corresponding MAME notifier phase.
The candidate callback is called after run_until and PCM capture when a new published field is observed; it is not an independently specified pre-IRQ input-sampling event.
